evidence.note: Systematic section-by-section reading of RFC 8878 up front — frame headers, FSE construction, Huffman weights, dictionary, FCS widths, predefined tables, repeat offsets — saving chunks to files and reading them methodically before/while implementing each subsystem.

When decoding failed, re-read the RFC reverse-bitstream section (lines 700-775) and reasoned explicitly about MSB/LSB stack ordering to correct the bit-read logic, grounding understanding in spec text rather than guessing.

Heavy hex-dump reconnaissance: dd/od on real .zst frames cross-referenced against decoder state, plus standalone C programs (fsetest8-12, spread2/3) to verify FSE table spread/state math against observed bytes — the level-8 cross-check-against-real-frames behavior.

Byte-level reasoning about repeat-offset prev_offsets indexing, ml_baseline+extra-bits budgets, and reserved-bit validity (0x3f) to detect it was parsing at a wrong offset — precise field-level model grounded in the spec.

Careful reasoning about FSE probability/repeat-flag handling and re-reading RFC lines 575-620 when spread computation diverged; some of this deep understanding arose reactively during debugging rather than being anticipated up front, keeping it below level 10.

reasoning: The agent reads the relevant RFC sections systematically before and during implementation, extracts the exact rules for the hard areas (FSE build, Huffman weights, FCS widths, repeat offsets), and repeatedly cross-checks them against hex dumps of real frames and standalone verification programs — squarely the level-8 description. It stops short of 9-10 because several key spec details (bitstream ordering, reserved bits) were discovered reactively through failure rather than a fully anticipated up-front model, and no explicit bit-level contract was documented.
